1.why: All eight screens are static, card-based pages with no animation, video, or pop-up elements.

2.why: Primary actions are solid blue buttons and the active control gets a high-contrast orange outline, although the dark Logs panel also competes for attention.

3.why: Each page shows a single centered card with one task so the needed field and button are immediately visible, though the delivered codes sit only in the Logs block at the bottom.

4.why: The user must track a six-step sequence, copy two delivered codes, and apply a five-part password rule, which imposes a heavy memory and procedure load.

5.why: No screenshot anywhere in the flow shows a password manager, autofill, or 'remember me' option.

6.why: No saved account or familiar identifier is ever presented; the user only handles unfamiliar code strings that must be copied or retyped.

7.why: Headings and instructions are plain one- or two-sentence text, with only the security notice and monospace log lines adding density.

8.why: Only success feedback appears (green confirmation, 'Password updated'); no error message describing a problem and its fix is ever shown.

9.why: Pages describe formats ('six-digit', '12 or more characters, including uppercase...') but never provide a sample value or worked example of what to type.

10.why: The offered options (open simulated reset link versus enter recovery code manually) are clearly labelled buttons, but no choice among password, code, or face login methods exists.

11.why: No screen presents more than one input field plus two buttons at a time, so the user is never faced with many simultaneous choices.

12.why: Each action produces visible feedback (green 'instructions have been prepared' message, new log entries per delivery, final 'Password updated' screen), though key outcomes like the codes appear only in the technical Logs panel.

13.why: Each new step includes short guidance, such as the password-composition rule and the persistent 'Keep your account safe' advice.

14.why: Fields remain editable and step 3 offers a Back button, but no error-and-retry path is demonstrated in the screenshots.

15.why: Every step reuses the same header, card layout, button styles, security panel, and Logs panel, making the interface consistent and learnable.
